We need a graph on 15 vertices with vertex-connectivity at least 3.  
A simple way to guarantee this is to make the graph 3-regular (each vertex degree 3) and ensure it is 3-vertex-connected.  
A 3-regular graph on an even number of vertices exists, and 15 is odd, so a 3-regular simple graph is impossible because the sum of degrees would be odd.  

However, vertex-connectivity at least 3 does not require regularity — we can have higher-degree vertices.  
A complete graph \( K_5 \) has connectivity 4, and we can attach the remaining 10 vertices in a way that maintains connectivity ≥ 3.  

A straightforward construction:  
Take a complete graph on 5 vertices (0–4).  
Add vertices 5–14, each connected to three distinct vertices from 0–4, ensuring no vertex in 0–4 gets overloaded.  
Since the core \( K_5 \) is 4-connected and each new vertex has 3 connections into it, removing any 2 vertices still leaves the graph connected.
